anti_overlap: Does NOT cover EMA arithmetic (fd-ema-float-accumulation-parity), regex patterns (fd-regex-compilation-unicode-fidelity), mutex design (fd-fingerprint-concurrency-model), or mirroring text output (fd-mirroring-instruction-determinism)
decision_lens: Every JSON field name mismatch between Go struct tags and Python dict keys is a data corruption vector during the concurrent operation period — Go reads Python-written fingerprints and must deserialize every field correctly or silently zero-initializes it, corrupting the EMA state
focus: Audits all JSON struct tags in Fingerprint, ModeProfile, Observables, and Cadence against the Python dict keys in _empty_mode_profile() and _empty_fingerprint() for wire compatibility during the concurrent operation period
name: fd-json-wire-compatibility-struct-tags
persona: Protocol compatibility engineer who has maintained dual-write JSON schemas across Python/Go service migrations with zero-downtime requirements
review_areas: ModeProfile field coverage: Python's _empty_mode_profile() defines 15 keys: n, avg_words, capitalization_ratio, emoji_density, pct_contraction, pct_question, pct_period, pct_exclamation, pct_lowercase, pct_multi_sentence, laughter, affirmation, intensifier, hedge, opener — every Go struct field must have a json tag matching exactly, with no omitempty on numeric fields that are intentionally 0.0

Vocabulary counter type: Python stores laughter/affirmation/intensifier/hedge/opener as dicts of {string: int}. Go must use map[string]int with json tag 'laughter' (not 'laughter_counts' or 'vocab_laughter') — and the zero value must serialize as {} not null, requiring explicit initialization in the empty constructor

Fingerprint top-level keys: Python's _empty_fingerprint() has message_count (int), global (dict), modes (dict of mode→profile), cadence (dict). Go Fingerprint must not rename 'global' to 'Global' — 'global' is a Go keyword so the struct field must be named differently (e.g., Global) but with json:"global" tag

Cadence sub-struct: Python cadence has avg_burst_size (float, default 1.0) and burst_count (int, default 0). Go Cadence struct must not omit avg_burst_size when it equals 0.0 — use json:"avg_burst_size" without omitempty, or Python reads a missing field as whatever json.loads returns for absent keys (KeyError or .get default)

Modes map key namespace: Python modes keys are the 7 mode strings ('emotional', 'analytical', 'playful', 'intimate', 'logistics', 'update', 'general'). Go Mode type must round-trip through JSON as these exact strings — if Mode is an iota int, its MarshalJSON must return the string value, not the integer

Null vs empty object serialization: Python initializes modes as {} (empty dict) and adds keys on first message for that mode. Go must serialize modes with no entries as {} not null — encoding/json marshals nil maps as null but initialized empty maps as {} — the Go Fingerprint constructor must use make(map[Mode]*ModeProfile) not var modes map[Mode]*ModeProfile

severity_examples.condition: BuildMirroring falls back to global profile which is always empty in Go's view, producing no mirroring instructions for all users during the concurrent operation period
severity_examples.scenario: The Go struct field for 'global' profile is named All or Profile to avoid the keyword collision but the json tag is accidentally omitted or set to 'all' — Python writes 'global' but Go deserializes into a zero-value struct, silently discarding the accumulated global profile on every read

severity_examples.condition: Vocabulary counters oscillate between absent and present depending on which language wrote last, corrupting laughter/affirmation/intensifier/hedge tracking
severity_examples.scenario: ModeProfile vocabulary counter fields have omitempty tags — when the user has never used laughter tokens, the laughter field is absent from Go's JSON output; Python reads this fingerprint and laughter.get() returns the absent-key default, but then update_fingerprint() overwrites the field with {} on next write, discarding what Python had accumulated

severity_examples.condition: Python crashes reading Go-written early fingerprints, breaking the concurrent operation period for new users
severity_examples.scenario: Go serializes the modes map as null when no mode-specific profiles exist yet (first 3 messages all general), because the Fingerprint was constructed with var modes map[Mode]*ModeProfile — Python's json.loads reads null as None and fingerprint['modes'] = None causes AttributeError on modes.get(current_mode)

success_hints: Golden JSON fixture generated from Python for a 10-message sequence; Go Unmarshal of that fixture followed by Marshal back to JSON; byte-comparison of the round-tripped JSON against the original (modulo key ordering); explicit test that modes serializes as {} not null for a fresh Fingerprint; Mode type has MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON tested with all 7 values plus an unknown value
task_context: During the concurrent operation period (benl.2 through benl.11), Python Auraken and Go Skaffen both read and write the same core_profiles.style_fingerprint JSONB column. JSON wire compatibility is the primary correctness requirement of this port — stated explicitly in the brainstorm. Python dict keys from _empty_mode_profile() (15 keys) and _empty_fingerprint() (4 keys) are the authoritative field names. Go struct tags must match exactly. 'global' keyword collision requires explicit tagging.
